prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glue degraders

statement.case_for: Having read all eight opening ballots, I move from my own opening to the targeted protein degradation candidacy. It has the broadest support across members with differing outlooks (six of eight rank it) and it describes a mechanism in chemical terms. A bifunctional molecule or a glue induces a ternary complex, ubiquitin is transferred, and the target is degraded by the proteasome. Cereblon as the thalidomide target gives the glue strand a defined molecular explanation. The idea has been confirmed independently over more than two decades, and degraders are now in late-stage clinical trials. As Secretary I also value that the attribution can be stated in committee language: Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated the PROTAC concept, and Handa identified cereblon, which explains the glue degraders. Handa is the natural third name because the discovery of a molecular target underpins the glue strand.
statement.case_against: The two strands, PROTACs and molecular glues, may be distinct discoveries, and three seats exclude Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure and rational design), Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, each with a credible claim. The first PROTAC work used peptidic, cell-impermeable molecules, so the decisive chemical step to drug-like degraders came later and from other hands. No PROTAC drug is yet approved, so the field is still moving. I would want the expert report to say what remains unsettled before we commit to a citation that spans both strands.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation is a simple, consequential chemical idea that opens the undruggable proteome, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa as the natural trio.
responses.response: I agree with the trio and with the scientific case, but I would not call the maturity question closed. Approval of a degrader is still pending and the catalytic ubiquitin-transfer mechanism in ternary complexes is understood in outline rather than in kinetic detail. I still think the chemistry is established enough. My own opening put Ciulli in the third seat, and I now accept that Deshaies has the stronger claim on priority for the original PROTAC concept. Ciulli's structural and design work is what I would reserve for the citation text.

responses.point: Base editing turns a Cas9 scaffold into a programmable deaminase and is a defined chemical reaction on one nucleotide, with large impact and wide reproduction, ranked first.
responses.response: I respect the chemistry, but I place it below degraders for two reasons. First, the 2020 prize for CRISPR-Cas9 is a close precedent, and the committee would have to justify that base editing is a distinct chemical achievement rather than an extension. Second, the attribution is the weak point. Naming Liu's two trainees alongside him is unusual, Liu alone is a plausible alternative, and Nishida and Kondo's Target-AID is a contemporaneous line that we cannot dismiss. I keep it as my first alternative because the evidence from clinical use is strong and the committee could reasonably prefer it.

responses.point: Phase separation is a new physical-chemical organizing principle of the cell, with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as the founding observation and multivalency framework.
responses.response: I ranked it last of those I listed, and I will say why instead of simply dismissing it. The concept is real and the physical-chemistry framing is attractive, but whether condensates are functionally general in vivo is still debated. I see a gap between the thermodynamic description in vitro and demonstrated mechanism in cells. I also think the credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is less settled than the three-name trio suggests. I would want the expert report to address in vivo evidence before I could support it.

responses.point: Massively parallel sequencing and nanopore reading of nucleic acids are physics-meets-chemistry advances that read genomes at scale and could be recognized.
responses.response: I do not think sequencing is weak science, but I would ask what the new chemistry is. Sanger was honored in 1980, and for Solexa the reversible-terminator chemistry has plural origins that make a three-person split hard to defend. For nanopores, the concept and the practical enzyme-controlled reading come from different groups, and I am uncertain that the committee agrees on who made reading practical. I take your point that the principle of single-molecule electrical readout appeals physically, and I would give nanopores more weight than sequencing-by-synthesis, but neither seems to me ahead of degraders on clarity of attribution.

uncertainties: Whether PROTACs and molecular glue degraders should be one prize part or whether the glue strand (Handa) is a separate achievement that complicates the citation.
Whether Deshaies or Ciulli should take the third seat if Handa is judged to belong to a different strand.
What the expert reports say about the state of mechanistic understanding of ternary complexes and the lack of an approved PROTAC.
Whether the committee views base editing as sufficiently distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. My research on respiratory proton and electron transfer is close to B020 (Gray and Winkler), which is why I judge that candidacy as a specialist and have not made it my preferred configuration. I have no personal or institutional connection to the degrader candidates. I note that I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, which is not relevant to any shortlisted candidate.
